question:
The requirement is to have the macro executed so that it loops through each and inserts data I cannot create a model due to the huge number of columns

I have created macros below and run dbt command as

dbt run-operation generate_insert_sql

But it just ran and nothing got executed

-- generate_insert_sql

 {% set c = ["COL_A", "COL_B", "COL_C", "COL_D", "COL_E"] %}

{% for c1 in c %}
    {% for c2 in c if c2 != c1 %}
        {{ generate_insert_sql(c1, c2) }}
    {% endfor %}
{% endfor %}

{% macro generate_insert_sql(c1, c2) %}
    INSERT INTO TABLE_A (
        cols,aggr_cols
    )
    SELECT cols, aggr_cols
      FROM TABL_2
    ) as a
    WHERE c1_type = '{{ c1 }}' AND c2_type = '{{ c2 }}'
    GROUP BY ALL;
{% endmacro %}
title: DBT:Executing macros as standalone doesn't run anything
answer: dbt macros don't inherently run SQL code. You can use the built-in run_query macro, or a statement block to actually run your SQL code.
